lesson.menu_title: Talking About Time — The Year After Everything Changed

lesson.subtitle: Lesson 10 -- Talking About Time

lesson.grammar_point: past perfect and past perfect continuous in narrative

listenings.text: Thank you. I will keep this to two minutes, which is about a minute and a half longer than anybody wants after dinner. When I started here I was twenty-six, and I had already been told by two people that the job would not last. By the time I finished, I had worked in this building for thirty-one years, under four presidents, and I had moved offices nine times without ever moving floor. What I want to say is this. For most of those years I had been arriving home at ten at night, and I had told myself it was temporary, and it was not. I am not going to pretend I would do it all again the same way. But I would do most of it, and I would do it with the same people, which is the part nobody writes into a career plan. Thank you for that.

When people tell the story of their own life in a second language, they almost always produce a list. I did this, then I did that, then I moved here. The list is accurate and nobody listens to it, including the person telling it. Here is what changes it, and it is one grammatical move. Put one thing behind another. Instead of I worked there for thirty years and then I retired, say by the time I retired I had been working in the same building for thirty years. Suddenly there is a shape, because the listener can hear which event is the frame and which one is the background. English does this constantly and speakers of other languages often do not, and it is the single clearest difference between a story and a list. One more thing. You do not need many of these. Two in a two minute story is plenty. What you are buying is not decoration, it is depth.

extra_audio.text: Carol asks Braulio how long he had been at the company when he decided to stop. He answers that by the time he finished he had been there for thirty-one years, and that he had told himself for most of them that the hours were temporary. Carol says that the first six months of her own retirement were the hardest, because nobody had warned her about the Tuesdays. Braulio asks her what changed after that. She tells him that she stopped trying to fill the time and started choosing what to put in it.

paras: Nobody prepares you for the Tuesdays. People prepare you for the money, and sometimes for the health, and everybody has an opinion about the hobby you are supposed to find. Nobody mentions that on the second Tuesday of the first free month you will stand in your own kitchen at eleven in the morning with nothing that has to be done, and that the feeling will not be relief.

Part of what is happening is arithmetic. By the time most people stop, they have been working for something close to forty years, and for most of those years they had been getting up before the alarm they set. The structure was not something they chose. It was the water. Take it away and the day does not become free; it becomes shapeless, which is a different thing, and it takes about a year to tell the difference.

The second part is harder to name. Work answers a question before you have asked it, and the question is what you are for. Nobody who has spent thirty years being needed at eight in the morning is ready for the silence of not being needed at eight in the morning. This is not depression and it is not ingratitude. It is a transition, and transitions have a shape: an ending first, then an empty middle that everybody underestimates, then a beginning that arrives later than promised.

The people who come out of it well seem to do one thing in common. They stop trying to fill the time and start choosing what to put in it, which sounds like the same sentence and is not. In hindsight, the empty middle was never the problem. The problem was expecting to skip it.
reading.source: Article -- The Long View, a newsletter about work and what comes after it

choices: Retirement is a financial problem that people plan badly for

items: The article says the feeling on that free Tuesday morning is relief.
The feeling will not be relief.
It says the structure of a working day was something people chose.
The structure was not something they chose. It was the water.

An ending first, then an empty middle that everybody underestimates, then a beginning that arrives later than promised.
